# Futures (inverse)

  * Updated September 25, 2025 12:43

Bitcoin futures on Deribit are cash settled rather than settled by physical delivery of BTC. This means that at expiration, the buyer of BTC futures will not buy the actual BTC, nor will the seller sell BTC. There will only be a transfer of profits/losses between the two opposing sides of the trade. When the contract expires, the expiration price is calculated as the 30 minute time weighted average price (TWAP) of the BTC index.

ETH futures work in the same way, but use the ETH index.

# Standard Margin Requirements by Instrument

This page shows, for each perpetual and future, the maximum position size (Max Amount), the maximum leverage, and the initial margin (IM) and maintenance margin (MM) requirements at key position sizes in Standard Margin accounts (S:SM and X:SM).

All values are calculated from the Standard Margin leverage formula, the instrument tiers, and the Max Amount listed on each contract specifications page. If any value here differs from those pages, the Standard Margin page and the contract specifications take precedence.

To check the requirements for an exact position size or a whole portfolio, use the Position Builder.

## How to read the tables

  * Max Amount is the maximum allowed position size for the instrument.

  * Max leverage is available for any position up to the size shown (the tier's constant maximum leverage range, C_{3}, multiplied by Max Amount). Above that size, available leverage decreases gradually.

  * 25%, 50% and 100% of Max Amount show the position size, the available leverage, and the IM and MM requirements at that size.

### Tip

You can review standard margin requirements for a simulated portfolio in the Position Builder.

## Margin calculations for futures and perpetuals in Standard Margin (SM) accounts

$$IM=\frac{1}{L(N)}$$

$$MM=\frac{2}{3}·IM$$

Where L(N) is the available IM leverage for the given coin and position size, calculated as:

$$L(N)={C}_{1}·{\left(\frac{{C}_{1}}{{C}_{2}}\right)}^{-\mathrm{M}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{x}{(0,\frac{\frac{N}{{N}_{Max}}-{C}_{3}}{1-{C}_{3}})}^{{C}_{4}}}$$

Where

C_{1} = Start leverage

C_{2} = End leverage

C_{3} = Constant maximum leverage range

C_{4} = Steepness factor

N = Position size in the account, measured in units of the underlying e.g. BTC

NMax = Max Amount, the maximum allowed position size, measured in units of the underlying e.g. BTC. Max Amount for each instrument is listed on the relevant contract specifications page.

## Instrument tiers

The values for C_{1}, C_{2}, C_{3}, and C_{4}, are set according to which tier an instrument is in. The parameter values for each tier are shown in the following table.

Tiers  | Start Leverage C_{1}  | End Leverage C_{2}  | Extended Leverage C_{3}  | Steepness C_{4}
Tier 1  | 50  | 4  | 5%  | 0.40
Tier 2  | 50  | 4  | 4%  | 0.40
Tier 3  | 50  | 2  | 4%  | 0.40
Tier 4  | 25  | 4  | 3%  | 0.35
Tier 5  | 25  | 2  | 2%  | 0.30
Tier 6  | 10  | 2  | 2%  | 0.25

Every linear crypto perpetual on Linear Perpetual is assigned to a tier below. Inverse BTC and ETH perpetuals use the same tier as the corresponding linear contracts. Dated futures are listed in a separate table.

Tiers  | Instruments (Perpetuals)
Tier 1  | BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP
Tier 2  | LTC, PAXG, HBAR, DOT, EURC
Tier 3  | AAVE, ADA, ENA, UNI, HYPE, LINK, APT, COIN50, COMP, DASH, ETC, ICP, POL
Tier 4  | TRX, NEAR, ALGO, AVAX, DOGE, BNB, 1000PEPE, APE, ARB, ATOM, ONDO, RENDER, SEI, SUI, TIA, XLM
Tier 5  | BCH, 1000SHIB, ALT, ASTER, BERA, CRV, DYDX, FARTCOIN, FIL, INJ, LDO, MEGA, MON, OP, PUMP, STRK, TAO, TOWNS, WIF, WLD, XPL, ZEC, PONS
Tier 6  | TRUMP, 1000BONK, 1000MOG, AERO, AVNT, BASED1, BILL, BOME, CFX, CHIP, EDGEX, EIGEN, ETHFI, FET, INX, JASMY, JTO, JUP, LIT, MERL, MORPHO, NIGHT, OPG, OPN, PENDLE, PENGU, PNUT, PRL, PYTH, RESOLV, ROBO, RUNE, S, SAGA, VIRTUAL, VVV, W, WLFI, CASHCAT

Tiers  | Instruments (Futures)
Tier 4  | BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, HYPE
Tier 6  | TRX, AVAX, BTCDVOL

RWA perpetuals (equities, equity ETFs, commodities and pre-IPO contracts) are not tiered in the tables above. Their maximum leverage is set per contract type, as described in RWA Perpetual.

## Maximum position sizes (Max Amount)

Max Amount is the NMax term in the leverage formula above. For the value of each instrument, see the relevant contract specifications page, or Standard Margin Requirements by Instrument for all instruments with their resulting leverage and margin requirements. These values apply from 24 September 2026 at 09:00 UTC.

  * Linear perpetuals

  * Linear futures

  * Inverse perpetuals

  * Inverse Futures

  * DVOL futures

  * RWA perpetuals

## Calculation example

Let’s say we are trading the linear BTC perpetual. BTC perpetuals are a tier 1 instrument, so from the above tables and the relevant contract specs, we know that:

C_{1} = 50

C_{2} = 4

C_{3} = 5%

C_{4} = 0.4

Max Amount (N_{MAX}) = 1,769

If we assume a position size of 150 BTC (N = 150), we can calculate the maximum IM leverage with the following formula:

$$L(N)={C}_{1}·{\left(\frac{{C}_{1}}{{C}_{2}}\right)}^{-\mathrm{M}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{x}{(0,\frac{\frac{N}{{N}_{Max}}-{C}_{3}}{1-{C}_{3}})}^{{C}_{4}}}$$

$$L(N)=50·{\left(\frac{50}{4}\right)}^{-\mathrm{M}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{x}{(0,\frac{\frac{150}{1769}-5\%}{1-5\%})}^{0.4}}$$

$$L(N)\approx 25.51$$

So with a position size of 150 BTC, we can open a position at roughly 25.51x leverage. 

IM = 1 / L(N)

IM = 1 / 25.51

IM ≈ 0.0392 = 3.92%

The IM requirements would then be this 3.92% multiplied by the position size of 150 BTC, so around 5.8800 BTC.

MM = 2/3 * IM

MM = 2/3 * 5.8800 BTC

MM = 3.9200 BTC

## Contract size

The contract size of an inverse future is denominated in USD, not in the coin that is used for margin and settlement. One BTC future contract represents 10 USD of exposure and one ETH future contract represents 1 USD, while the resulting profit, loss and margin are denominated in BTC and ETH respectively.
